From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@nimbus.ai>

Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:23:12 -0700
Subject: MAP and procurement timelines — potential drift

Hi Jonas,

Quick heads-up from procurement: they reviewed the MAP and want a SOC 2 excerpt + a short runbook of data handling before legal will allow the PO to be raised. That adds an extra internal review and will likely push signature beyond our previously agreed close (end of May).

We still want to move forward — the product eval went well — but procurement says their earliest signature window is now mid-June unless we can provide the requested evidence and a short bridging plan. Can you confirm:
- Can Redwood provide the SOC2 excerpt (control mappings) and a short runbook by EOD tomorrow?
- If we accept a limited pilot (no production data) while procurement finishes their review, can Redwood hold pricing and the Q3 go-live commitment?

Appreciate a quick read on options; this affects our launch planning.

Thanks,
Aisha
Sr. Product Manager, Nimbus.ai
[aisha.khan@nimbus.ai]

[Attachment: procurement_requirements_20260520.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 10:05:34 -0700

Hi Aisha — thanks for the flag and the procurement doc. Quick answers below and a proposed bridging approach.

Short answers:
- Yes, we can produce a redacted SOC 2 excerpt and a 2-page data handling runbook by EOD tomorrow. I attached the excerpt we usually share with procurement.
- We can support a limited pilot (sandbox/obfuscated data) with the current pricing locked for 30 days while procurement completes. To preserve the Q3 commitment we'd like a nominal written acknowledgment (email) from procurement that the pilot is in-scope.

Proposed next steps (can do immediately):
1) Share SOC2 excerpt + runbook (EOD 5/21) — attached.
2) Execute a short pilot MAP amendment (provisional MAP v3) that lists pilot boundaries and acceptance criteria — I can share a one-page addendum today.
3) If procurement needs a pricing hold beyond 30 days, we can authorize a limited credit hold (finance sign-off required) — will escalate internally.

If this approach sounds reasonable I’ll loop in Marissa (rev credits & approvals) and Legal for the MAP addendum. Can we do a 30-minute sync tomorrow at 11am PT?

Best,
Jonas
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0118

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding the procurement ask from Nimbus. Key points:
- Procurement wants SOC2 snippet + runbook — we can deliver by EOD 5/21.
- Customer requests a pricing hold for the period procurement is reviewing; they’d run a limited pilot in the meantime.
- They indicated signature could slide to mid-June without the bridging items.

Requesting:
1) Fast approval for a 30-day pricing hold and a provisional credit (nominal) if procurement pushes beyond 30 days. This is to prevent losing committed go-live window.
2) Quick review by Legal to confirm we can issue a one-page MAP addendum that limits pilot scope (no production PII) and keeps pricing locked.

I’ll set up a quick sync with Nimbus — propose 5/21 11am PT.

Thanks,
Jonas

Thanks for the summary, Jonas. I agree with the proposed approach — delivering the SOC2 excerpt and a narrow runbook is standard and should satisfy procurement. Approvals:

- Pricing hold: approve a 30-day hold on list pricing while procurement completes their review. If procurement requests >30 days, we will assess a small pre-approved credit (up to 5% of first-year committed ARR) — finance to confirm.
- MAP addendum: Legal should prepare a 1-page pilot addendum limiting the pilot to non-production data and a hard stop if any compliance redlines appear. Karthik, can you loop Legal?
- Escalation: If procurement needs exec sign-off, I will own the escalation and join a call with their VP of Procurement.

Please proceed to share the addendum and SOC artifacts with Nimbus; tag me on the HubSpot thread when done. Keep the pilot acceptance criteria tight (success metrics + exit criteria).
